evidence.note: Guarded.env was checked against the trust-boundary claim in docs/fsm/driving-a-workflow.md: the child env is exactly {PATH,HOME,LANG,TMPDIR} present in the parent, plus MRV_RUN_ID, plus the declared names. No shadowing escape exists: internal/fsm/workflow/workflow.go:117-118 reserves PATH/HOME/LANG/TMPDIR and the MRV_/LD_/DYLD_/GIT_ prefixes, so a workflow cannot declare an env name that overrides MRV_RUN_ID or the loader variables. Doc and code agree.

Output-cap arithmetic verified end to end: cappingWriter retains at most MaxOutput+1 bytes and keeps draining (returns len(p), nil, so the pipe never blocks), and exec's `len(res.Stdout) > MaxOutput` at line 153 detects overflow precisely because of that extra byte. Stdout/Stderr are separate cappingWriters on separate pipe goroutines, so there is no shared-buffer race.

Error classification reviewed for mis-audit: on a runner error data.ExitCode is forced to unknownExit and data.Error carries errs.Code(err) (ERR_CMD_TIMEOUT survives); a spawn failure with no code is wrapped as ERR_CMD_FAILED{reason:spawn}. Pre-exec refusals (not consented, relative argv[0], ERR_CMD_CHANGED from workflow.VerifyCmds) leave data.Name empty and are correctly never audited (lines 176-180, 194-196). The exec runner's switch checks ctx.Err() before tctx.Err(), so a parent cancellation is never mislabelled a timeout, and a kill-vs-exit race at the deadline still classifies as ERR_CMD_TIMEOUT.

The new test file is fixture-safe against metareview's own lints: the work marker (line 22), its fingerprint (line 23) and the unsafe-call string (line 24) are assembled from concatenated fragments, so neither the quality:todo lint nor the security:eval lint fires on this diff itself while the fixtures still drive the lints under test. go test ./internal/reviewers/... passes at 97.0% statement coverage.

gitStatus separates presence from version correctly (Present stays true for an old git), MinGitVersion 2.31 matches the `git >= 2.31` prerequisite stated in the new docs/fsm/driving-a-workflow.md, and atLeastVersion's field-by-field compare returns the right answers on the boundary cases I hand-checked (2.39.5 >= 2.31 true, 2.30.9 false, bare "2" false). internal/setup/gitversion_test.go covers the seam cases; go vet and go test are clean for the package (86.7% coverage).

AppendJSONL's named-return + deferred closeFile pattern is correct: the marshal/write error wins (`cerr != nil && err == nil`), the early MkdirAll return shadows deliberately before any file exists, and internal/state/state_test.go:11-42 covers both branches (Close error surfaced; Close error not masking the marshal error). ReadJSONL's `_ = file.Close()` on the read-only path is justified.

The doc's factual claims were spot-checked against shipped code rather than trusted: exit 1 for DONE(reviewed) is internal/fsm/machine/machine.go:865-867 (StatusDone defaults to 0, OutcomeReviewed sets ExitCode 1); --repair, --accept-workflow-change, --include-vars, --at-iter, --allow-custom-cmds are real flags (internal/fsm/cli/run.go:87,113); ERR_VAR_FROZEN, ERR_FORK_INCOMPLETE, ERR_RUN_LOCKED, ERR_AUDIT_FULL, ERR_AUDIT_TORN all exist; audit.torn-*.bin (internal/fsm/run/store.go:38) and runs/.torn/ (internal/fsm/machine/machine.go:346) are real paths. No doc-vs-code drift found.

findings.note: Read/write asymmetry in the JSONL cap. ReadJSONL now admits lines up to maxJSONLLineBytes (internal/state/state.go:66), but AppendJSONL (state.go:28-50) enforces no matching limit, so a record that marshals to more than 1 MiB is written happily and then makes the ENTIRE file unreadable: scanner.Scan stops and internal/state/state.go:78 returns bufio.ErrTooLong, so every callsite (internal/taskdone/review.go:239, internal/prready/review.go:262, internal/epicready/review.go:204, internal/artifactreview/review.go:149, internal/learning/*) loses the whole run/finding history rather than one row. The change is a strict improvement over the previous 64 KiB default and current run records are far below 1 MiB, so this is a durability observation, not a regression — but a symmetric cap (or skipping an over-long line instead of failing the read) would close it.

evidence.note: read cap raised to maxJSONLLineBytes+2

A single round-trip test with a ~100 KiB record would pin it.

findings.note: Dead field: Guarded.Clock (internal/fsm/cmdexec/cmdexec.go:77) is never read anywhere in the package — grep for Clock in internal/fsm/cmdexec returns only the declaration — yet internal/fsm/cli/deps.go:90 populates it on every constructed Guarded. Event timestamps are in fact stamped centrally by session.audit (internal/fsm/machine/machine.go:466), so the field is a vestige. Harmless today, but a reader of cmdexec's audit path is invited to assume cmd_call carries a cmdexec-controlled clock when it does not.

findings.note: parseGitVersion (internal/setup/setup.go:224) returns whatever token follows the literal word "version", with no check that the token looks like a version. Output such as "not a version banner" yields Version="banner", so gitStatus stores a bogus Version and rejects it only as a side effect of atLeastVersion's strconv.Atoi failure, producing the misleading operator message "Upgrade git: metareview fsm needs git >= 2.31, found banner." instead of the intended "Could not parse the git version" branch at setup.go:211 — which is consequently unreachable for that class of input. A leading-digit check on the candidate token would route it correctly.

evidence.note: no shape check on the token after "version"
the parse-failure branch is bypassed by such input
wrong message: reports the garbage token as a found version

findings.note: The git-version verdict influences no machine-readable signal. missingFullMetaswarmPrereqs (internal/setup/setup.go:254-267) inspects only Beads/Metaswarm/Superpowers Present flags, and cmd/metareview/main.go:420-424 prints the report and returns with exit 0 regardless, so `metareview setup --check` reports standalone.fullMetaswarmReady exactly the same for a git 2.20 as for a git 2.50 — only the free-text Action and versionOk fields carry the warning. This is consistent with the pre-existing design (an entirely absent git is also not in that list and also exits 0), so I am not treating it as a regression introduced here; flagged because an operator scripting on exit status or on fullMetaswarmReady still gets a clean setup and then hits the FSM failure this check was added to prevent.

evidence.note: readiness ignores git entirely, version or not
setup --check always exits 0

findings.note: The production branch of gitStatus is untested. internal/setup/gitversion_test.go injects the gitVersionOutput seam in every case, so the default closure at internal/setup/setup.go:198-201 — exec.Command(status.Path, "version").Output(), the one line that decides whether the check works on a real machine, and the only caller shape used by Check at setup.go:90 — is never executed by the suite. I confirmed manually that the real path works (`go run ./cmd/metareview setup --check` reports the local git version and VersionOK true), so this is regression risk rather than a defect.
